title: Mangled CSV Import
concept: Hand-rolled CSV parsing: quoting, header normalisation and blank lines
symptom: Importing the supplier file gives three problems: 'Smith, Jane' is split into two columns, the 'Name ' header with a trailing space can't be looked up as 'name', and the blank line at the end of the file becomes an empty record.
rootCause: Three independent bugs from parsing CSV by hand. split(',') cannot see quotes, so a comma inside a quoted cell starts a new column. Header names are used as typed, with stray spaces and capitals. Nothing skips blank lines, so a trailing newline becomes a row with no data.

wrongFixes.whyWrong: `if not line` only catches a completely empty line. A line holding spaces is still truthy, so it is parsed into a bogus record.

turns.text: Import is broken for the supplier file, three tests fail.
Switch to the csv module for quoting, normalise headers with strip().lower(), and skip empty lines.
All three cases now pass, so the importer is fixed.

transcript.verdict: Two of the three fixes are right, but the blank-line check treats only truly empty lines as blank. Files exported from spreadsheets often end with whitespace-only lines, which still become records.

grading.question: Why is split(',') not a CSV parser?
grading.ideal: It ignores quoting, so commas inside quoted cells are treated as separators.

grading.question: What is the difference between `not line` and `not line.strip()`?
grading.ideal: The first is only true for an empty string; the second is also true for a line of whitespace.
